About / Thakorn Tangphadungrutch

Curiosity, built
into practice.

I am a student engineer, researcher, and community builder exploring how robotics, artificial intelligence, and mechanical design can address real-world challenges.

The longer story

Theory. Practice.
People.

I am a secondary student at Brentwood School in the United Kingdom, having previously studied at the British International School Ho Chi Minh City. I am most engaged when I can move between theory and practice: understanding how a system works, building a prototype, testing it under real constraints, and explaining the result clearly to others.

That approach has shaped my work across robotics, artificial intelligence, and mechanical design. For a rescue-drone project, I completed 60 laboratory flights and three outdoor field trials. I later developed a smart life-jacket prototype connecting location tracking and drift-direction prediction with the goal of drone-supported rescue. In research, I led a team studying AI applications in Vietnam’s stock market and collaborated on deep-learning-based optimization of a small gas turbine compressor.

I also care about how technical knowledge is shared. I founded STEM GEARS, developing ten 3D-printed cutaway aircraft-engine models and STEM kits for younger learners. The venture sold 60 products and generated VND 100 million in revenue, all donated to Creativism Club and SafeFlow Vietnam. Through DRONEVERSE, SafeFlow, and PhyX, I have helped make engineering, water safety, and STEM learning more accessible.

Across these experiences, I have learned to value iteration, evidence, teamwork, and responsibility. A strong project should be tested honestly, communicated accessibly, and connected to a meaningful need.
